policy: Historical associations are evidence-qualified; no blanket sacred designation. Modern analytical profiles are not evidence of ancient species or recipes.

entries.evidence_type: FTIR on mummy skin, hair and wig
entries.period: New Kingdom context, TT71 area (1479–1458 BCE)
entries.description: FTIR was interpreted as frankincense with juniper resin. This method does not establish a Boswellia species or a complete recipe. Modern B. carterii chemistry is stored separately.

entries.evidence_type: Classical/Egyptian textual comparison and experimental archaeology
entries.period: Ptolemaic/Roman textual and Mendesian perfume context
entries.description: The Mendesian perfume reconstruction uses myrrh. Ancient terminology and modern species assignment require caution; a reconstructed recipe is not direct proof of each ingredient in Cleopatra’s perfume.
entries.taxonomic_scope: Commiphora resin interpretation; no ancient C. myrrha species determination

entries.description: Ricinoleic-acid patterns were interpreted as castor oil in workshop residues. Degradation and mixture context constrain inference; not evidence that the free acid was the original whole oil.

entries.evidence_type: Proteomics primary study with archaeological synthesis
entries.period: Second millennium BCE / New Kingdom reference context
entries.confidence: Moderate for regional crop; indirect for Egypt
entries.description: The primary proteomics results concern Levantine dental calculus. The discussion regards Tutankhamun-tomb sesame seeds as credible based on prior archaeobotany. This is indirect Egyptian evidence, not Egyptian oil residue identification.
entries.taxonomic_scope: Species-supported regional proteins; Egyptian claim derives from cited archaeobotany

entries.evidence_type: Microscopy and chemical study of museum archaeological textiles
entries.period: Pharaonic to Ptolemaic; individual textile dates in source Table 1
entries.confidence: High for linen use; oil use not tested
entries.description: Flax-derived linen shrouds and mummy textiles establish botanical/funerary use. They do not demonstrate that linseed oil was used as an embalming ingredient.
entries.taxonomic_scope: Flax textile fibres; modern seed-oil profiles separate

entries.period: Pharaonic Egyptian museum textiles; sample dates in Table 1
entries.confidence: High for dye material; oil use not tested
entries.description: Six textile samples contained safflower dye markers. This supports dye use and funerary textiles, not sacred status or safflower oil use.

entries.evidence_type: Experimental archaeology and historical oil-name interpretation
entries.description: Balanos is evaluated in the perfume reconstruction literature. Historical plant-name translation and reconstruction are less specific than direct botanical remains; modern kernel-oil data do not establish ancient use.

entries.evidence_type: Multianalytical residue study including plant DNA
entries.period: Ptolemaic-style Bes vase; original find context unrecorded
entries.description: The study reports Nymphaea nouchali var. caerulea in a museum Bes vessel. Ritual and psychoactive interpretations are hypotheses; the vessel lacks a secure excavated provenance. No synthetic modern chemical profile was added.
entries.taxonomic_scope: Source taxon N. nouchali var. caerulea / N. caerulea synonym context

entries.confidence: High for conifer preparation; unresolved genus pair
entries.description: Biomarkers support juniper/cypress oil or tar in workshop preparations. They do not securely separate these genera or establish J. phoenicea as the ancient species.
entries.taxonomic_scope: Juniperus/Cupressus unresolved; modern J. phoenicea reference separate

entries.confidence: High for cedar-derived material; species unresolved
entries.description: Cedar tar marker patterns were detected in two canopic jars. Modern C. atlantica tar was a reference; this does not identify ancient cedar to that species.
entries.taxonomic_scope: Cedrus genus; no ancient species assignment

entries.description: Plant oil interpreted as olive-type is reported among workshop preparations. Common fatty-acid patterns, degradation and mixtures limit species specificity.
entries.taxonomic_scope: Probable olive-type oil; not species-exclusive biomarkers

entries.evidence_type: Historical oil-name interpretation; no direct molecular species proof
entries.period: Ancient Egyptian oil texts, chronology varies
entries.description: The source discussion explicitly notes that baq oil may refer to olive, moringa or another oil plant. No secure M. peregrina-specific ancient residue identification is claimed. Modern Omani seed-lipid data remain separate.
entries.taxonomic_scope: Candidate Moringa identification; cannot substitute M. oleifera
